description.en: First Weeks. Your first class: one easy round to learn five basic moves. Stop each one well before it gets hard.
First Weeks. Gentle pushing and support holds, so your wrists and shoulders get used to your weight.
First Weeks. Legs and trunk at an easy pace. Learn each shape, there is no need to push.
First Weeks. Hangs and rows on the bar. Short hangs start building the grip your pull-ups will need.
First Weeks. Trunk basics on the floor. Slow, controlled reps teach your body to stay firm and still.
First Weeks. One easy round of the basics. Keep the same steady pace from the first move to the last.
First Weeks. An easy walk and gentle trunk drills. You should finish fresher than you started.
First Weeks. The first circuit again, now two rounds. Same easy reps, rest as long as you need.
First Weeks. Your first hold with your hips over your hands, feet on a box. Keep it short and easy.
First Weeks. The legs circuit again, now two rounds at the same easy reps.
First Weeks. A little longer on the bar, and two more rows a set than last week.
First Weeks. Box-pike holds first, then the trunk work. Squeeze your legs together in every hold.
First Weeks. Two rounds of the basics, with a few more reps than in week one.
First Weeks. A longer walk, then slow spine drills and long breaths out to settle after two weeks.
First Weeks. A few more reps on every move. Leave two in reserve on each set.
First Weeks. Box-pike holds get a little longer. Press the floor away and keep your arms straight.
First Weeks. Side planks join the legs circuit. Keep your hips high and your body straight from head to feet.
First Weeks. A third set of hangs and rows. Squeeze your shoulder blades together before each row.
First Weeks. Tomorrow is your first test. One easy set of each today, so you arrive fresh.

First Weeks. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Bodyweight Squat.
Floor Push-Ups. An easy walk and light leg work after the test. A gentle day for your wrists.
Floor Push-Ups. Your first floor push-ups: two sets of three. Stop with two reps in reserve.
Floor Push-Ups. A third box-pike hold today. Push tall through straight arms the whole time.
Floor Push-Ups. Knee raises from a hang join the legs circuit. Lift slowly, with no swinging.
Floor Push-Ups. Longer hangs and ten rows a set. Keep your body straight like a plank on every row.
Floor Push-Ups. Bear crawls join the trunk work. Knees just off the floor, small steps, back flat.
Floor Push-Ups. Floor push-ups replace incline ones in this circuit too. Still three reps a set.
Floor Push-Ups. Walk, then easy ankle and hip drills to free up your squat.
Floor Push-Ups. Dips with your feet helping on the floor. Lower only as far as your shoulders feel good.
Floor Push-Ups. Box-pike holds reach twenty seconds. Rest fully so every hold stays clean.
Floor Push-Ups. Your first third round, on the legs day. Same reps as before, just one more lap.
Floor Push-Ups. Your first pull-up negatives: start at the top and lower yourself slowly, three seconds down.
Floor Push-Ups. A third hollow hold and longer bear crawls. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor in the hollow.
Floor Push-Ups. Assisted dips join this circuit too. Two rounds, still well short of tiring.
Floor Push-Ups. Walk, then slow shoulder and upper-back drills. Move gently and never into pain.
Floor Push-Ups. A third round on the pull and push circuit. Same reps, more work in total.
Floor Push-Ups. Steady holds today, and incline push-ups go up to eight a set.
Floor Push-Ups. Reverse lunges replace split squats. Step back softly and keep your front knee over your foot.
Floor Push-Ups. Tomorrow is a test day. Easy single sets only, nothing close to hard.

Floor Push-Ups. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Push-Up.
Wall & Negatives. Walk your hands along the bars while you hold yourself up. Small steps, shoulders down.
Wall & Negatives. A long easy walk and slow trunk drills. Breathe out fully on every rep.
Wall & Negatives. Pull-ups with your feet helping on the floor. Chest to the bar, then lower slowly.
Wall & Negatives. Your first chest-to-wall handstand: walk your feet up the wall, hold, then walk back down.
Wall & Negatives. A few more squats and lunges each round. Keep every rep slow and even.
Wall & Negatives. Negatives slow to four seconds down. Stay in control until your arms are straight.
Wall & Negatives. Your second wall handstand day. A little longer on the wall, then the trunk work.
Wall & Negatives. This circuit gets its third round too, with five push-ups a set.
Wall & Negatives. An easy walk and light leg work. A calm day for your wrists and elbows.
Wall & Negatives. Five reps a set on pulls, push-ups and dips. Every rep slow and full.
Wall & Negatives. Learn to come out of a handstand safely: turn and step down to one side.
Wall & Negatives. Squats reach eighteen a set. Breathe steadily and keep your heels down.
Wall & Negatives. Small swings on the bar, moving between hollow and arch shapes. Short and controlled.
Wall & Negatives. Wall handstands grow to fifteen seconds. Push tall and keep your eyes on your hands.
Wall & Negatives. Push-ups go to six a set. If your form breaks, end the set there.
Wall & Negatives. Walk, then slow hip and ankle drills. Let your legs recover from the squat work.
Wall & Negatives. Six reps on push-ups and dips, and longer hollow holds. Keep the same calm pace.
Wall & Negatives. Your first frog stand: knees on your elbows, lean until your feet lift. Five seconds is plenty.
Wall & Negatives. Tomorrow is a test day. One easy set of each, then rest up.

Wall & Negatives. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Chest-to-Wall Handstand.
First Pull-Up. Your first tuck L-sit: press down through straight arms and lift your hips, knees tucked.
First Pull-Up. Seven push-ups a set now. Take a longer rest when you need it to keep your form.
First Pull-Up. Walk, then gentle shoulder drills. Nothing today should feel like work.
First Pull-Up. Assisted pull-ups reach six a set and push-ups seven. Keep every rep smooth.
First Pull-Up. Your first pike push-ups: hips high, lower your head toward the floor just in front of your hands.
First Pull-Up. Twenty squats a set, and lunges go to ten per leg. Keep an even pace.
First Pull-Up. One try at a strict pull-up from a dead hang, then slow negatives.
First Pull-Up. Wall handstands reach twenty seconds. Keep the L-sit holds short and clean.
First Pull-Up. Eight push-ups a set. The same three rounds, with a little more in each.
First Pull-Up. A long walk and slow trunk drills, with long breaths out to relax your back.
First Pull-Up. Push-ups and dips gain a rep, and hollow holds grow to thirty-five seconds.
First Pull-Up. Your first slow dip negatives: start at the top and take five seconds to lower.
First Pull-Up. Cossack squats replace lunges. Shift side to side, only as deep as feels easy.
First Pull-Up. Another strict pull-up try, then negatives at five seconds down.
First Pull-Up. Wall handstands reach twenty-five seconds, and the L-sit holds get a little longer.
First Pull-Up. Rows with your feet raised on a box, a harder angle. Fewer reps to start.
First Pull-Up. Walk, then light leg and wrist care. Take it easy before the test week.
First Pull-Up. Nine push-ups and eight dips a set. Hold your best form through the whole round.
First Pull-Up. Three wall holds today, and frog stands grow to eight seconds.
First Pull-Up. Tomorrow you test your first strict pull-up. Easy single sets today.

First Pull-Up. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Strict Pull-Up.
Foundations Finale. Your first thirty-second wall handstand. If you tip off the wall, turn out with the side exit.
Foundations Finale. Squats reach twenty-two and rows go to eight. Steady breathing all the way through.
Foundations Finale. Walk, then ankle and hip drills. A quiet day before the last block of the level.
Foundations Finale. A strict pull-up single in every round, then assisted pull-ups for the extra reps.
Foundations Finale. Your first kick-ups to the wall: three soft ones per leg. Turn out sideways if you go too far.
Foundations Finale. Pause for two seconds at the bottom of each squat. Fewer reps, more control.
Foundations Finale. Chin-ups, palms facing you, join three strict pull-up singles.
Foundations Finale. Two half-minute wall holds, and the tuck L-sits grow to twelve seconds.
Foundations Finale. Ten push-ups a set, this level's push-up goal. Make every one of them clean.
Foundations Finale. Walk, then shoulder and upper-back drills. Loosen up for the last two weeks.
Foundations Finale. Strict singles again, now with five assisted pull-ups a round.
Foundations Finale. Two sets of kick-ups per leg and ten-second frog stands. Stay relaxed on the way up.
Foundations Finale. Paused squats reach ten, and cossack squats get one more rep per side.
Foundations Finale. Two chin-ups a set and slower negatives. The last hard bar day of the level.
Foundations Finale. The last balance day of the level: the same holds, with cleaner shapes.
Foundations Finale. The last engine circuit of the level. Ten push-ups a set, all of them clean.
Foundations Finale. A long easy walk and slow breathing. Two days to the level test.
Foundations Finale. Tomorrow is the level test. One easy set of each, and plenty of rest tonight.

Foundations Finale. One clean set of each skill the level trained, at the belt you reached, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Strict Pull-Up.
Bar Basics. An easy restart after the level test. Short sets with plenty left in reserve.
Bar Basics. Split squats with your back foot up on a bench. Go slow and find your balance first.
Bar Basics. Frog stands and foot-assisted dips, the base for your first bar dips next week.
Bar Basics. Handstand day, easy on the elbows. Practise going up and coming down, then press overhead.
Bar Basics. An easy bar day of hangs and rows, building the grip your pull-ups need.
Bar Basics. All the basics in one class. Pull-ups move up to sets of two from today.
Bar Basics. An easy walk and light leg work, the first rest day of the new level.
Bar Basics. Pull day, with no handstands. Pull-ups and slow negatives come first, while you are fresh.
Bar Basics. Tempo week: lower every squat and split squat over three seconds. Same reps as last week.
Bar Basics. Your first dips on the bars: three sets of three. Lower only to a depth that feels good.
Bar Basics. One more exit per side. Stay relaxed on the wall and keep your arms long.
Bar Basics. Hold yourself on top of a bar with straight arms and a firm trunk, a first step toward the muscle-up.
Bar Basics. Bar dips replace assisted dips on the basics day, still at three a set.
Bar Basics. Walk, then slow hip and ankle drills to keep your squat moving freely.
Bar Basics. Your first tuck lever rows: under a low bar, knees tucked, feet light, draw your hips up.
Bar Basics. A third set of split squats. Keep your front heel down on every rep.
Bar Basics. Bar dips go to four a set and push-ups to eleven. Rest fully between sets.
Bar Basics. Four kick-ups per leg now, and pike push-ups go to seven a set.
Bar Basics. Tomorrow is the first test of the level. One easy set of each, nothing more.

Bar Basics. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Strict Pull-Up.
Pull-Up Strength. Walk, then gentle shoulder drills after the test. Nothing today should strain.
Pull-Up Strength. A chin-up set now follows the pull-ups, so you pull a little more without longer sets.
Pull-Up Strength. Candlestick rolls: roll onto your upper back, stack your hips, roll down slowly. Keep weight off your neck.
Pull-Up Strength. Tempo week: three seconds down on every dip and push-up.
Pull-Up Strength. Your first German hang: feet on the floor, roll back under a low bar until your hands are behind you.
Pull-Up Strength. Straight-leg raises from an active hang replace knee raises. Lift slowly, without swinging.
Pull-Up Strength. The hardest class of the week. A chin-up set joins the basics, every rep smooth and full.
Pull-Up Strength. A longer walk, then slow spine drills and long breaths out.
Pull-Up Strength. Tuck lever rows go to five a set. Hold the tucked shape tight at the top.
Pull-Up Strength. Tempo week on the legs: three seconds down, the same reps as last week.
Pull-Up Strength. Five bar dips and twelve push-ups a set, and longer frog stands.
Pull-Up Strength. Pike push-ups reach eight a set. Keep your hips high and your elbows pointing back.
Pull-Up Strength. Tempo week on the bar: slow leg raises and rows, and longer support holds.
Pull-Up Strength. The week's hard day, and the last basics day before the test. Dips and push-ups gain a rep.
Pull-Up Strength. An easy walk and light leg work. A gentle day for your wrists and elbows.
Pull-Up Strength. Tempo week on the bar: three seconds down on every pull-up and row.
Pull-Up Strength. Single-leg bridges replace the two-leg version. Keep your hips level as you lift.
Pull-Up Strength. The same doses as last time. Make every dip and push-up a little cleaner.
Pull-Up Strength. Tomorrow is a test day. One easy set of each, then stop while you feel fresh.

Pull-Up Strength. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Strict Pull-Up.
First Lever. Pull-ups go to sets of three. Rest a full two minutes between sets.
First Lever. Walk, then slow hip and ankle drills. A quiet day before your first lever.
First Lever. Your first tuck front lever: under the bar, knees tucked, hips up near shoulder height. Five seconds.
First Lever. More split squats per leg and longer trunk holds. Steady and controlled.
First Lever. Bar dips reach six a set. Keep your shoulders down and your chest up.
First Lever. Your longest wall holds yet, three of forty seconds, and five kick-ups per leg.
First Lever. Your first low-bar transitions: with your legs helping, move from below the bar to support on top.
First Lever. Tempo week, and the week's hard day: three seconds down on every pull-up and dip.
First Lever. Walk, then easy shoulder and upper-back drills. Move slowly and breathe.
First Lever. The same five-second lever holds, then slow pull-ups and leg raises.
First Lever. Squats reach twenty-four, and candlestick rolls go to six, lowered slowly.
First Lever. Your first planche lean: from a plank, shift your shoulders just past your hands, elbows straight.
First Lever. In your wall handstand, press through your fingers until your toes go light for a moment.
First Lever. Tempo week on the bar. Handstand exits move to this day for the rest of the level.
First Lever. The week's hard day. A chin-up set returns after the pull-ups, and wall holds reach forty seconds.
First Lever. A long easy walk and slow trunk drills to recover from the week.
First Lever. Lever holds go to six seconds, and a chin-up set follows the pull-ups.
First Lever. Tempo week on the legs, three seconds down. Tuck L-sits go to three sets.
First Lever. Leans grow to ten seconds. Push the floor away and keep your arms locked.
First Lever. Two sets of toe pulls now. Find the light moment, then settle back onto the wall.
First Lever. Tomorrow you test your first lever. One easy set of each today, and no lever holds.

First Lever. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Tuck Front-Lever Hold.
Lean & Press. An easy walk and light leg work after the test.
Lean & Press. Tempo week: slow pull-ups and leg raises, with the same six-second lever holds.
Lean & Press. Squats reach twenty-five and split squats ten per leg. Keep the pace even.
Lean & Press. Seven bar dips and fourteen push-ups a set. Frog stands reach twenty seconds.
Lean & Press. Pike push-ups reach ten a set. Keep your hips stacked high over your hands.
Lean & Press. Your first partial skin-the-cat on a low bar, feet nearby. Turn only as far as your shoulders allow.
Lean & Press. The week's hard day: dips go to seven a set and push-ups to fourteen.
Lean & Press. Walk, then easy hip and ankle drills. A calm day for your legs.
Lean & Press. Lever holds reach seven seconds. Keep your arms straight and your back flat.
Lean & Press. Your first supported pistols: hold something secure and sit down on one leg, three per side.
Lean & Press. Leans grow to twelve seconds. Lean only as far as your arms stay straight.
Lean & Press. Three kick-up sets per leg and longer toe pulls. Stay calm while your toes go light.
Lean & Press. Tempo week on the bar: slow leg raises, longer support holds and one more transition.
Lean & Press. The week's hard day, at the same doses as last time. Make each rep cleaner.
Lean & Press. Walk, then shoulder and upper-back drills. A quiet day before the test week.
Lean & Press. Tempo week: slow pull-ups and rows, with seven-second lever holds.
Lean & Press. Tempo week on the legs: three seconds down on squats and pistols.
Lean & Press. Tempo week: three seconds down on dips and push-ups, and a third set of frog stands.
Lean & Press. The same holds and kick-ups as last time. Smooth on the way up and down.
Lean & Press. An easy day of basics at half effort. Keep plenty in reserve for the test.
Lean & Press. Tomorrow is a test day. One easy set of each, and no lever holds today.

Lean & Press. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Planche Lean.
Bar Strength Finale. An easy restart after the test. Short sets, and rows to keep your pulling going.
Bar Strength Finale. Your first one-leg L-sit: one leg straight out at hip height, the other tucked. Five seconds a side.
Bar Strength Finale. Eight bar dips and fifteen push-ups a set, the top numbers of this level.
Bar Strength Finale. Tempo week: three seconds down on pike push-ups. Wall holds reach forty-five seconds.
Bar Strength Finale. One more skin-the-cat rep and one more exit per side. Move slowly through each turn.
Bar Strength Finale. Pull-ups go to sets of four. The chin-up set drops out to make room.
Bar Strength Finale. An easy walk and light leg work. Two weeks left in the level.
Bar Strength Finale. Lever holds reach eight seconds, and pull-ups stay at sets of four.
Bar Strength Finale. Tempo week on the legs, and one more second on each one-leg L-sit.
Bar Strength Finale. Tempo week: slow dips and push-ups. Leans reach fifteen seconds.
Bar Strength Finale. Toe pulls grow to twenty-five seconds. Breathe slowly while you balance.
Bar Strength Finale. The last bar day of the level, at a slow tempo. Smooth and controlled throughout.
Bar Strength Finale. The last basics day before the level test. Same doses, your best form.
Bar Strength Finale. Walk, then easy hip and ankle drills. Two days to the level test.
Bar Strength Finale. Tomorrow is the level test. One easy set of each and no lever holds.

Bar Strength Finale. One clean set of each skill the level trained, at the belt you reached, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Strict Pull-Up.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. An easy first day back: short holds and light basics after the level test.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Legs and core at the numbers you finished Level 2 with, nothing new today.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: pseudo-planche push-ups, two short sets with the shoulders leaning past the hands.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Kick up to the wall, pull your toes off it, then press pike push-ups for the shoulders.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Bar day: partial skin-the-cats and the German hang open the shoulders for the back lever.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Pull-ups, dips and push-ups in steady sets, with a wall handstand first.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. An easy day: a walk and slow upper-back drills to loosen the shoulders.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Tuck front lever holds come first while you are fresh, then pull-ups and low-bar transitions.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: the single-leg Romanian deadlift, a slow hinge on one leg for the hamstrings.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Frog stand and planche lean as last week, and one more rep on the pseudo-planche push-ups.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: seated pike lifts, raising straight legs off the floor to build compression.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: the flag support, side-on to the pole with the feet on the floor, the first flag step.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. One more pull-up rep in each set and a rep more on the push-ups.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. An easy walk and slow core drills for the spine, then long breathing on the floor.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. The tuck front lever holds go up a second, with pull-ups at five reps.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: the partial shrimp squat, the back foot held up, lowering only part of the way.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. The frog stand and lean hold a little longer, and dips and push-ups add a rep.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. New today: pike push-ups with the feet raised on a box, a step closer to the handstand push-up.
Kick-Ups & Toe Pulls. Light half sets of tomorrow's tests and an easy German hang, then rest well.

First Skills, block 1. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Pseudo-Planche Push-Up.
First Balance. An easy day after the exam: a walk, calf raises and slow wrist circles.
First Balance. Ten-second tuck front lever holds today, then transitions and pull-ups.
First Balance. New today: the full L-sit, both legs straight out in front, in short five-second holds.
First Balance. Pseudo-planche push-ups climb to six reps, the holds stay as last week.
First Balance. The last week of kick-ups and toe pulls before free balance attempts start.
First Balance. New today: dips on a straight bar, the top half of the muscle-up, in two short sets.
First Balance. New today: kick up away from the wall and try to balance for a few seconds, exits first.
First Balance. An easy day: a long walk, ankle rocks and slow hip switches.
First Balance. Tuck front lever holds reach eleven seconds, and the transitions add a rep.
First Balance. Balance attempts move onto the legs day too, and squats go up to thirty reps.
First Balance. The frog stand and lean hold a little longer today.
First Balance. Balance attempts replace the kick-ups on the press day: three short tries after the exit drill.
First Balance. Slow three-second lowering on the leg raises and rows, and ten-second flag supports.
First Balance. Elevated pike push-ups replace the floor pike here, and push-ups reach sixteen.
First Balance. An easy walk and slow rotations to free the upper back.
First Balance. Slow three-second pull-ups and leg raises this week, the tuck lever held at eleven seconds.
First Balance. A rep more on the single-leg RDL and a second more on the balance attempts.
First Balance. Push-ups go up to seventeen, the holds stay as last week before the exam.
First Balance. Half sets of tomorrow's tests and an easy German hang, nothing hard today.

First Skills, block 2. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: L-Sit.
Bar Strength. An easy day after the exam: short holds, light basics and a gentle German hang.
Bar Strength. A second easy day before the new block: a walk and slow core drills.
Bar Strength. Pull-ups go up to six reps and the tuck lever to twelve seconds.
Bar Strength. Assisted pistols and partial shrimps add a rep, and the L-sit holds seven seconds.
Bar Strength. A little longer on the frog stand and lean, and dips reach ten reps.
Bar Strength. Nine-second balance attempts and a longer wall hold before the pressing.
Bar Strength. Three sets of the flag support and four straight-bar dips a set, ready for the tuck flag next week.
Bar Strength. New today: chest-to-bar pull-ups, pulling higher until the chest touches the bar.
Bar Strength. An easy walk with calf raises and glute bridges, and gentle wrist work.
Bar Strength. Chest-to-bar pull-ups join the pull day, two sets of two after the tuck lever.
Bar Strength. New today: the bent-knee dragon flag negative, lowering slowly from the shoulders for four seconds.
Bar Strength. A third set of pseudo-planche push-ups today, and the frog stand a second longer.
Bar Strength. Ten-second balance attempts and a rep more on the elevated pike push-ups.
Bar Strength. New today: the tuck human flag with one foot on the floor to help, five seconds a side.
Bar Strength. Pull-ups move to six reps and dips to ten, the handstand work as before.
Bar Strength. An easy day: a long walk and slow hip and ankle drills.
Bar Strength. New today: the band-assisted muscle-up, pulling over the bar with a band taking some weight.
Bar Strength. Slow three-second lowering on the single-leg work, and the L-sit reaches eight seconds.
Bar Strength. Push-ups reach eighteen, and the frog stand and lean hold a second longer.
Bar Strength. New today: handstand push-up negatives, lowering slowly from a wall handstand for five seconds.
Bar Strength. New today: the full skin-the-cat, turning all the way through between the hands and back.
Bar Strength. The wall hold goes up to fifty-seven seconds and the elevated pike push-ups add a rep.
Bar Strength. An easy day before the exam: a walk and slow shoulder drills.

First Skills, block 3. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Tuck Front-Lever Hold.
First Back Lever. An easy day after the exam: short holds, light legs and a few slow candlesticks.
First Back Lever. Pseudo-planche push-ups go to seven reps and the frog stand a second longer.
First Back Lever. A third set of handstand push-up negatives and eleven-second balance attempts.
First Back Lever. New today: the tuck back lever, face down behind the bar, two short five-second holds.
First Back Lever. Balance attempts reach eleven seconds, the basics stay as last week.
First Back Lever. An easy walk and slow core drills, then long breathing on the floor.
First Back Lever. New today: the muscle-up negative, lowering slowly from the top of the bar for five seconds.
First Back Lever. Seven reps on the assisted pistols and six on the partial shrimps.
First Back Lever. Dips reach eleven reps, and the holds stay to let the shoulders settle.
First Back Lever. Elevated pike push-ups go up to eight reps, the negatives stay at three sets of two.
First Back Lever. A third set on the tuck back lever and the assisted tuck flag, still five seconds each.
First Back Lever. Pull-ups go up to seven reps and push-ups to eighteen.
First Back Lever. An easy walk, calf raises and glute bridges, with gentle wrist work.
First Back Lever. Thirteen-second tuck front levers and a third rep on the band muscle-ups.
First Back Lever. Nine-second L-sits and nine reps a side on the single-leg RDL.
First Back Lever. Thirty-second frog stands and twenty-second leans, the numbers the tuck planche needs next level.
First Back Lever. Twelve-second balance attempts and a full minute on the wall.
First Back Lever. An easy day: one short tuck back lever hold, light basics and a dead hang.
First Back Lever. Half sets of tomorrow's tests: pull-ups, push-ups, dips and leg raises.

First Skills, block 4. One clean set of each skill at the belt you reached in the last three weeks, in order: balance, holds, strength, basics, trunk. Rest fully between tests. Missing the headline or three targets offers a block repeat. Headline: Tuck Back Lever.
Level Test. An easy day after the exam: short holds, light basics and a straight-bar support.
Level Test. Dragon-flag negatives go to four reps and balance attempts to twelve seconds.
Level Test. The frog stand and lean keep their new times, with push-ups at nineteen.
Level Test. Three reps in each set of handstand push-up negatives now, five seconds down each.
Level Test. Six-second tuck back lever holds and six seconds a side on the assisted tuck flag.
Level Test. Steady basics this week: seven pull-ups, eleven dips and eighteen push-ups a set.
Level Test. An easy walk and slow rotations for the upper back and shoulders.
Level Test. Fourteen-second tuck front levers and a third rep on the muscle-up negatives.
